claim: The olfactory placode has been classically presumed to form all olfactory sensory neurons in vertebrates.
source_text: Classically, it has been presumed that the olfactory placode forms all olfactory sensory neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This statement refers to established scientific consensus in the field prior to this study.

claim: The cranial neural crest is the primary source of microvillous sensory neurons within the olfactory epithelium of zebrafish embryos.
source_text: In contrast, we show that the cranial neural crest is the primary source of microvillous sensory neurons within the olfactory epithelium of zebrafish embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches including photoconversion-based fate mapping, live cell tracking, and laser ablation.

claim: Neural crest precursors that coexpressed Sox10 protein and a neurogenin1 reporter ingressed into the olfactory epithelium and differentiated into microvillous sensory neurons.
source_text: A subset that coexpressed Sox10 protein and a neurogenin1 reporter ingressed into the olfactory epithelium and differentiated into microvillous sensory neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by live imaging data showing coexpression of Sox10:eGFP and Ngn1:nRFP in cells that ingress and differentiate.

claim: Sox10 plays a critical role in microvillous neurogenesis.
source_text: Timed loss-of-function analysis revealed a critical role for Sox10 in microvillous neurogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by morpholino knockdown experiments showing loss of microvillous neurons when Sox10 is depleted.

claim: The olfactory epithelium has a remarkable ability to regenerate neurons in adult organisms.
source_text: This knowledge is critical for understanding not only disorders such as anosmia—the loss of smell—but also for clarifying the remarkable ability of the olfactory epithelium to regenerate neurons in adult organisms
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations (Graziadei and Graziadei, 1979; Bermingham-McDonogh and Reh, 2011) and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The peripheral nervous system of the vertebrate head is derived from two sources: cranial ectodermal placodes and neural crest cells.
source_text: The peripheral nervous system of the vertebrate head is derived from two sources: cranial ectodermal placodes and neural crest cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt and Gans, 1983; Baker and Bronner-Fraser, 2001; Barraud et al., 2010).

claim: Placodes form the sense organs (nose, ears, and lens) of the head and contribute to neuronal portions of cranial ganglia.
source_text: Whereas placodes form the sense organs (nose, ears, and lens) of the head and contribute to neuronal portions of cranial ganglia, the glia are solely neural crest derived
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt and Gans, 1983; Baker and Bronner-Fraser, 2001; Barraud et al., 2010).

claim: Glia in cranial ganglia are solely neural crest derived.
source_text: the glia are solely neural crest derived
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Northcutt and Gans, 1983; Baker and Bronner-Fraser, 2001; Barraud et al., 2010).

claim: The olfactory placode first becomes apparent around 18 hr post-fertilization (hpf) in zebrafish embryos.
source_text: In the zebrafish embryo, the olfactory placode first becomes apparent around 18 hr post-fertilization (hpf)
evidence_reasoning: This timing is supported by citations (Hansen and Zeiske, 1993; Miyasaka et al., 2007).

claim: There are two predominant types of olfactory sensory neurons within the olfactory epithelium: ciliated and microvillous neurons.
source_text: Within the olfactory epithelium, there are two predominant types of olfactory sensory neurons: ciliated and microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about olfactory neuron classification.

claim: Ciliated sensory neurons are more basally located and detect volatile odorants.
source_text: Whereas more basally located ciliated sensory neurons detect volatile odorants
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Buck, 2000; Sato and Suzuki, 2001; Hansen and Zielinski, 2005) and represents established knowledge.

claim: Microvillous sensory neurons are more apically located and can detect pheromones, nucleotides, and/or amino acids, depending on the species.
source_text: more apically located microvillous sensory neurons can detect pheromones, nucleotides, and/or amino acids, depending on the species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Buck, 2000; Sato and Suzuki, 2001; Hansen and Zielinski, 2005) and represents established knowledge.

claim: Olfactory ensheathing glia are neural crest derived.
source_text: Recent literature demonstrates that olfactory ensheathing glia, nonneuronal supporting cells previously assumed to derive from the olfactory epithelium, are actually neural crest derived
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (Barraud et al., 2010).

claim: All other peripheral glia are neural crest derived.
source_text: These findings are consistent with the neural crest origin of all other peripheral glia
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (Woodhoo and Sommer, 2008).

claim: There has been considerable controversy over whether neural crest cells give rise to GnRH cells of the terminal nerve.
source_text: As one example, some studies (Whitlock et al., 2003; Forni et al., 2011) have suggested that neural crest cells give rise to GnRH cells of the terminal nerve, which is close to though not part of the olfactory nerve and epithelium. However, many other studies refute this notion and support a placodal origin for GnRH cells
evidence_reasoning: This controversy is documented through multiple citations representing both sides of the debate.

claim: Harden et al. (2012) interpreted their results to indicate a lack of contribution of neural crest cells to the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Harden et al. (2012) recently examined the interactions of Sox10:eGFP-positive cells with six4b:mCherry-expressing placodal precursors in zebrafish. The authors interpreted their negative results to indicate a lack of contribution of neural crest cells to the olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct statement about the interpretation of another study, supported by citation.

claim: Using the Sox10:eGFP line, this study definitively demonstrates the neural crest origin of microvillous neurons within the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: However, using the same Sox10:eGFP line, here we definitively demonstrate the neural crest origin of microvillous neurons within the olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data using the Sox10:eGFP transgenic line.

claim: Neural crest gives rise to microvillous, but not ciliated, sensory neurons in the developing olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Interestingly, we find that neural crest gives rise to microvillous, but not ciliated, sensory neurons in the developing olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data showing Sox10:eGFP-positive cells colocalize with TRPC2:Venus (microvillous marker) but not OMP:RFP (ciliated marker).

claim: A neurogenin1 (Ngn1) reporter and Sox10 protein are expressed in the subset of neural crest-derived nasal cavity cells that undergo dynamic ingression into the olfactory epithelium to form microvillous neurons.
source_text: Specifically, we demonstrate that a neurogenin1 (Ngn1) reporter and Sox10 protein are expressed in the subset of neural crest-derived nasal cavity cells that undergo dynamic ingression into the olfactory epithelium to form microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by live imaging data showing coexpression of Ngn1:nRFP and Sox10:eGFP in ingressing cells.

claim: If the neural crest is ablated, the olfactory epithelium cannot compensate for the loss of microvillous neurons.
source_text: If the neural crest is ablated, the olfactory epithelium cannot compensate for the loss of microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by laser ablation experiments showing persistent loss of microvillous neurons after ablation of Sox10:eGFP/Ngn1:nRFP-positive cells.

claim: The neural crest specifier gene Sox10 is required for microvillous neurogenesis as these cells are ingressing into the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Finally, we show that the neural crest specifier gene Sox10 is required for microvillous neurogenesis as these cells are ingressing into the olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by timed loss-of-function analysis using photo-morpholinos showing that Sox10 is required during the ingression period.

claim: Sox10:eGFP+ neural crest migrates dorsal to the eye and toward the olfactory region at 19 hpf as the olfactory placode is first apparent.
source_text: Sox10:eGFP+ neural crest migrates dorsal to the eye and toward the olfactory region at 19 hpf as the olfactory placode is first apparent.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in live imaging experiments as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A subset of nasal cavity cells that express Ngn1:nRFP ingress into the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Time-lapse confocal microscopy of live embryos (Sox10:eGFP+; Ngn1:nRFP+) demonstrates that a subset of nasal cavity cells that express Ngn1:nRFP (B, boxed area arrowheads; z = 3.5 μm) ingress into the olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in time-lapse confocal microscopy as shown in Figure 1B-D and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: All ingressing cells express Ngn1:nRFP.
source_text: All ingressing cells express Ngn1:nRFP (F, inset arrowhead).
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in live imaging data as shown in Figure 1F.

claim: At 53 hpf, all Sox10:eGFP+ cells in the olfactory epithelium are TRPC2:Venus+ microvillous neurons.
source_text: At 53 hpf, all Sox10:eGFP+ cells in the olfactory epithelium are TRPC2:Venus+ microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by colocalization of Sox10:eGFP and TRPC2:Venus markers in Figure 1K.

claim: Only a small number of microvillous neurons are not Sox10:eGFP+.
source_text: Only a small number of microvillous neurons are not Sox10:eGFP+ (arrowheads).
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in imaging data shown in Figure 1K and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Beginning at ∼24 hpf and continuing until at least day 2, a subset of the Sox10:eGFP-positive cells in the nasal cavity delaminated and intercalated into the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Subsequently, beginning at ∼24 hpf and continuing until at least day 2, a subset of the Sox10:eGFP-positive cells in the nasal cavity delaminated and intercalated into the olfactory epithelium where placode-derived ciliated neurons and support cells were already present.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed through time-lapse imaging as shown in Figure 1C-J and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Concomitantly with ingression, cells increased their eGFP levels and changed their morphology from mesenchymal to the 'teardrop' shape characteristic of neurons.
source_text: Concomitantly, these cells increased their eGFP levels and changed their morphology from mesenchymal to the 'teardrop' shape characteristic of neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1C-J and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: None of the Sox10:eGFP-positive cells within the olfactory epithelium are OMP:RFP-positive ciliated neurons.
source_text: In contrast, none are OMP:RFP-positive ciliated neurons (data not shown).
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as an observation from experiments crossing Sox10:eGFP with OMP:RFP lines.

claim: The ingressed Sox10:eGFP-positive cells are post-mitotic neurons as confirmed by HuC/D antibody staining.
source_text: To further confirm that the ingressed cells are neurons, we performed immunostaining with an antibody against HuC/D, a marker for newly born post-mitotic neurons (Kim et al., 1996), which colocalized in the apically located Sox10:eGFP-positive neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and the use of HuC/D as a neuronal marker is supported by citation (Kim et al., 1996).

claim: All neurogenic placodes in zebrafish, including the olfactory placode, express the proneural bHLH transcription factor Ngn1.
source_text: All neurogenic placodes in zebrafish, including the olfactory placode, express the proneural bHLH transcription factor Ngn1
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Andermann et al., 2002; Bertrand et al., 2002; Cau et al., 2002).

claim: Ngn1 is required for sensory neuron differentiation in mice.
source_text: which is known to be required for sensory neuron differentiation in mice
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Andermann et al., 2002; Bertrand et al., 2002; Cau et al., 2002).

claim: Ngn1 is expressed in neural crest cells that become sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia in zebrafish.
source_text: In addition, Ngn1 is expressed in neural crest cells that become sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia in zebrafish
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (McGraw et al., 2008).

claim: Ngn1:nRFP expression is observed in a subset of Sox10:eGFP-positive cells in the nasal cavity.
source_text: Using a Ngn1:nRFP transgenic line (Blader et al., 2003) that has been well-characterized as representative of endogenous Ngn1 expression (Blader et al., 2003, 2004; Madelaine et al., 2011), we noted Ngn1:nRFP expression in a subset of Sox10:eGFP-positive cells in the nasal cavity
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in imaging data (Figure 1B) and the transgenic line is validated by citations.

claim: Only cells that upregulate Sox10:eGFP and coexpress Ngn1:nRFP ingress into the olfactory epithelium to differentiate into microvillous neurons.
source_text: Interestingly, only cells that upregulate Sox10:eGFP and coexpress Ngn1:nRFP ingress into the olfactory epithelium to differentiate into microvillous neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in live imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Sox10 is not entirely neural crest specific and becomes downregulated with time in some lineages.
source_text: Although Sox10-driven lines mark neural crest cells, Sox10 is not entirely neural crest specific and becomes downregulated with time in some lineages
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established knowledge about Sox10 expression patterns.

claim: Highly stable eGFP often persists after Sox10 downregulation.
source_text: whereas highly stable eGFP often persists
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as a known property of eGFP protein stability.

claim: Photoconversion of neural crest cells at 14-16 hpf results in labeled cells in the nasal cavity at 29 hpf.
source_text: At 29 hpf, a few photoconverted cells were present in the nasal cavity
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 2D-E'.

claim: At 55 hpf, photoconverted neural crest cells had differentiated into apically localized microvillous neurons.
source_text: At 55 hpf, by which time ingression/differentiation was nearly complete, photoconverted neural crest cells had differentiated into apically localized microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 2F-G'.

claim: No photoconverted cells differentiate into the basally located ciliated neurons.
source_text: In contrast, no photoconverted cells differentiate into the basally located ciliated neurons, consistent with their placodal origin and confirming the specificity of our labeling.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photoconversion experiments (Figure 2F-G') and the inference about placodal origin is drawn from this observation.

claim: Many labeled neural crest cells cross the midline and migrate to the contralateral side where they differentiate into microvillous neurons.
source_text: Interestingly, many labeled neural crest cells cross the midline and migrate to the contralateral side (shown in Figure 2) where they differentiate into microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The small subset of microvillous neurons that are not Sox10:eGFP-positive show no overlap with the photoconverted Dendra2Red.
source_text: The small subset of microvillous neurons that are not Sox10:eGFP-positive show no overlap with the photoconverted Dendra2Red
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Laser ablation of Sox10:eGFP+/Ngn1:nRFP+ cells in the nasal cavity at 25 hpf results in a significant decrease in the number of Sox10:eGFP+/TRPC2:Venus+ microvillous neurons at 35 hpf.
source_text: 35 hpf embryos show a significant decrease in the number of Sox10:eGFP+/TRPC2:Venus+ microvillous neurons within the right olfactory epithelium as compared to the unablated left side in both small (C) and large (D) ablation experiments.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in laser ablation experiments shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: Directly adjacent ciliated neurons are only marginally affected by laser ablation of Sox10:eGFP+/Ngn1:nRFP+ cells.
source_text: Directly adjacent ciliated neurons are only marginally affected.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in laser ablation experiments shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: The placode-derived olfactory epithelium is unable to compensate for the loss of the neural crest–derived population of microvillous neurons.
source_text: Interestingly, the placode-derived olfactory epithelium is unable to compensate for the loss of the neural crest–derived population of microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from laser ablation experiments showing persistent loss of microvillous neurons without recovery.

claim: The Sox10:eGFP line exhibits a striking upregulation of eGFP expression in cells concomitant with their intercalation into the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: The Sox10:eGFP line exhibits a striking upregulation of eGFP expression in cells concomitant with their intercalation into the olfactory epithelium
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in live imaging data shown in Figure 1 and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Sox10:eGFP+ differentiating microvillous neurons colocalize with anti-Sox10 antibody staining at 26 hpf and 34 hpf.
source_text: Sox10:eGFP+ differentiating microvillous neurons in fixed embryos stained with anti-GFP antibody colocalize with anti-Sox10 antibody staining at 26 hpf (A and A') and 34 hpf (B and B').
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by immunostaining data in Figure 4A-B'.

claim: Levels of eGFP and Sox10 protein mirror each other, both increasing as cells ingress and become neurons.
source_text: Levels of eGFP and Sox10 mirror each other, both increasing as cells ingress and become neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A-B'.

claim: Loss of Sox10 leads to marked depletion of microvillous neurons in the olfactory epithelium.
source_text: The results show that loss of Sox10 leads to marked depletion of microvillous neurons in the olfactory epithelium
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by morpholino knockdown experiments in Figure 5.

claim: Sox10 morpholino-injected embryos display only slight changes in ciliated neurons, whereas microvillous neurons are significantly decreased in number and organization.
source_text: Embryos with mild and moderate phenotypes (assayed histologically) display only slight changes in ciliated neurons, whereas microvillous neurons are significantly decreased in number and organization.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 5B-C'.

claim: At 60 hpf, Sox10 morpholino-treated embryos demonstrate a persistent decrease in the number of microvillous cells and disorganization in comparison to control embryos.
source_text: Antibody staining with anti-GFP against TRPC2:Venus in fixed embryos demonstrates a persistent decrease in the number of microvillous cells and disorganization at 60 hpf in Sox10 morpholino-treated embryos (H) in comparison to control embryos (G).
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by immunostaining data in Figure 5G-H.

claim: All control morpholino-treated embryos have high pigmentation.
source_text: As expected, all control morpholino-treated embryos have high pigmentation
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in morpholino experiments shown in Figure 5J.

claim: All Sox10 morpholino-treated embryos with high pigmentation have only a mild phenotype.
source_text: and all Sox10 morpholino-treated embryos with high pigmentation have only a mild phenotype.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in morpholino experiments shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Sox10 morpholino treatment results in most embryos having either no microvillous neurons or a decreased number.
source_text: In all cases (J and K), Sox10 morpholino treatment results in most embryos having either no microvillous neurons or a decreased number.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in morpholino experiments shown in Figure 5J-K.

claim: Microvillous neuron reduction is a consistent and common feature across all categories after knockdown of Sox10.
source_text: Surprisingly, microvillous neuron reduction is a consistent and common feature across all categories after knockdown of Sox10.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed across all morpholino experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Microvillous neuron formation is exquisitely sensitive to reductions in Sox10 protein levels.
source_text: These data suggest that microvillous neuron formation is exquisitely sensitive to reductions in Sox10 protein levels, whereas other Sox10-dependent processes such as pigmentation may be more resilient.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that microvillous neurons are lost even in embryos with high pigmentation (mild Sox10 knockdown).

claim: Control embryos (not photocleaved) developed normal numbers and organization of olfactory sensory neurons at 38 hpf.
source_text: While control embryos developed normal numbers and organization of olfactory sensory neurons at 38 hpf
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photo-morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6A-A'.

claim: Embryos subjected to photocleavage at 24 hpf develop ciliated neurons but significantly lack microvillous neurons at 38 hpf.
source_text: identically injected embryos subjected to photocleavage at 24 hpf go on to develop ciliated neurons but significantly lack microvillous neurons at 38 hpf (B and B') in comparison to control embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in photo-morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6B-B'.

claim: Sox10 is required specifically during microvillous neurogenesis, as opposed to only during its earlier role in neural crest specification/migration.
source_text: To determine if Sox10 is required specifically during microvillous neurogenesis, as opposed to only during its well-established earlier role in neural crest specification/migration, we took advantage of a new photocleavable morpholino system
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by photo-morpholino experiments showing that Sox10 knockdown at 24 hpf (after neural crest migration) still prevents microvillous neuron formation.

claim: The role of Sox10 in microvillous neurogenesis is consistent with its role in regulating neuronal differentiation from neural crest of other peripheral sensory and autonomic neurons across species.
source_text: Interestingly, the role of Sox10 in microvillous neurogenesis is consistent with its role in regulating neuronal differentiation from neural crest of other peripheral sensory and autonomic neurons across species.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from comparing the current findings with established knowledge about Sox10's role in other neural crest lineages.

claim: Sox10 is required for formation of sensory, sympathetic, and enteric neurons as well as for glia and Schwann cells.
source_text: Sox10 is not only required for formation of sensory, sympathetic, and enteric neurons but also for glia and Schwann cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Britsch et al., 2001; Sonnenberg-Riethmacher et al., 2001; Carney et al., 2006; Kelsh, 2006).

claim: Sox10's expression in and specific effect on microvillous neurons within the first several hours of olfactogenesis demonstrate a direct effect on neurogenesis in the context of zebrafish olfactory development.
source_text: Data shown here, namely Sox10's expression in and specific effect on microvillous neurons within the first several hours of olfactogenesis, demonstrate a direct effect on neurogenesis at least in the context of zebrafish olfactory development.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the temporal and spatial specificity of Sox10 expression and function shown in the experimental data.

claim: It was long assumed that olfactory sensory neurons derive solely from the olfactory placode.
source_text: It was long assumed that olfactory sensory neurons derive solely from the olfactory placode
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established dogma supported by citations (Hansen and Zeiske, 1993; Whitlock and Westerfield, 2000).

claim: Two lineage analysis studies in mice suggested that a small subpopulation of unspecified olfactory sensory neurons may have a neural crest origin.
source_text: Although two lineage analysis studies in mice suggested that a small subpopulation of unspecified olfactory sensory neurons may have a neural crest origin (Forni et al., 2011; Katoh et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as findings from other studies, supported by citations.

claim: Wnt1-Cre and P0-Cre both suffer from lack of neural crest specificity.
source_text: they relied upon Wnt1-Cre and P0-Cre, both of which suffer from lack of neural crest specificity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a critique based on known limitations of these Cre lines, supported by subsequent citations about Wnt1 expression.

claim: The Wnt1 marker is not entirely neural crest specific, as it is also expressed in the dorsal neural tube, otic placode, and several other regions.
source_text: Interpretation of these experiments is made difficult by the fact that the Wnt1 marker is not entirely neural crest specific, as it is also expressed in the dorsal neural tube, otic placode, and several other regions
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Riccomagno et al., 2005; Liu et al., 2006; Freyer et al., 2011; Valenta et al., 2011).

claim: By using photoconversion of Sox10-expressing neural crest cells, this study was able to unequivocally follow individual neural crest cells from their site of origin in the dorsal neural tube to their ingression into the olfactory epithelium and differentiation into microvillous sensory neurons.
source_text: Here, by using photoconversion of Sox10-expressing neural crest cells, we were able to unequivocally follow individual neural crest cells from their site of origin in the dorsal neural tube to their ingression into the olfactory epithelium and differentiation into microvillous sensory neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by photoconversion experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Olfactory sensory neurons are notable for their regenerative capacity.
source_text: Olfactory sensory neurons are notable for their regenerative capacity.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established knowledge about olfactory neurons.

claim: In the case of placode-derived ciliated sensory neurons, their replenishment throughout the lifespan likely occurs within the mature olfactory vesicle.
source_text: In the case of placode-derived ciliated sensory neurons, their replenishment throughout the lifespan likely occurs within the mature olfactory vesicle.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of ciliated neuron renewal based on their placodal origin.

claim: There may be a subpopulation of microvillous sensory neurons derived from the olfactory vesicle.
source_text: Similarly, there may be a subpopulation of microvillous sensory neurons derived from the olfactory vesicle.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculation based on the observation of a small number of Sox10:eGFP-negative microvillous neurons.

claim: Given evidence of large-scale neural crest contribution to microvillous sensory neurons, their replacement during adulthood may take place via a latent neural crest stem cell population derived from the nasal cavity.
source_text: Alternatively, given our evidence of large-scale neural crest contribution to microvillous sensory neurons, it is intriguing to consider that their replacement during adulthood may take place via a latent neural crest stem cell population derived from the nasal cavity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative hypothesis about adult microvillous neuron renewal based on the embryonic neural crest contribution.

claim: During vertebrate evolution, a myriad of changes have occurred in olfaction, including the emergence of the vomeronasal organ, which fish and birds appear to lack.
source_text: During vertebrate evolution, a myriad of changes have occurred in olfaction, including the emergence of the vomeronasal organ, which fish and birds appear to lack.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established knowledge about evolutionary changes in olfactory systems.

claim: The reduction in microvillous neurons after the loss of Sox10 is accompanied by only minor effects on the placode-derived ciliated neurons with which they intermix.
source_text: Notably, the reduction in microvillous neurons after the loss of Sox10 is accompanied by only minor effects on the placode-derived ciliated neurons with which they intermix.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: There is no general loss of neurogenesis in the olfactory placode after Sox10 loss but rather a microvillous-specific phenotype.
source_text: Therefore, there is no general loss of neurogenesis in the olfactory placode but rather a microvillous-specific phenotype.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that ciliated neurons are largely unaffected while microvillous neurons are lost after Sox10 knockdown.

claim: An observed slight decrease in ciliated neuron numbers and thinning of projections in morpholino-treated embryos is likely a secondary effect due to the absence of normally adjacent microvillous neurons.
source_text: An observed slight decrease in ciliated neuron numbers and thinning of projections in morpholino-treated embryos, similar to that seen in the laser ablation experiments, is likely a secondary effect due to the absence of normally adjacent microvillous neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from comparing the effects in morpholino and laser ablation experiments.

claim: Ciliated neurons largely recover by 48 hpf development, whereas neural crest–derived microvillous neurons do not.
source_text: Ciliated neurons largely recover by 48 hpf development, whereas neural crest–derived microvillous neurons do not.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in time-course experiments following morpholino knockdown.
